endpoint: claude -p (Claude Code headless) with built-in WebSearch + WebFetch

freshness_overlay.brief_suffix: Only use sources published on or after {{AFTER_DATE}}.

query_transform_notes: The harness model writes its own queries; the brief is the shared extractor brief. WebSearch returns titles+URLs only (up to 8 backend searches per call); WebFetch runs a small-model extraction over the page (lossy by design).
cost_model: $10/1k searches + extractor-model tokens (WebFetch adds no tool fee). Searches capped at 10 per run via env cap; tokens dominate.

env.CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SES.note: Documented as a cap that 'can be raised'; lowering it below 200 is not documented as supported. Alternative: cap in the brief and audit the transcript.

billing per backend search.note: Docs: WebSearch 'may issue up to eight backend searches per call'; whether each is billed as one search is not stated.

top_k.note: Native harness has no top-k control; 10 is enforced by the brief ('read at most 10 pages') and audited.

docs.supports: WebSearch/WebFetch behavior, 200-search session cap, env vars, WebFetch 100k chars, 15-min cache

rationale.model: Pin the fixed extractor model so the reader is the same as other search arms (only possible when the extractor is a Claude model).
rationale.tools: Only WebSearch+WebFetch: the native retrieval surface; no MCP search.
